rules.when: The captain explicitly requests Codex, an independent second opinion, or an alternative implementation.
rules.why: Honor explicit routing requests and provide an independent perspective.

rules.when: GPU and real-time video pipeline work that needs deep systems reasoning: writing or optimizing CUDA kernels, GPU memory management (unified/pinned/zero-copy, NvBufSurface), TensorRT engine building or custom plugins, DeepStream pipeline architecture, custom GStreamer elements or DeepStream plugins in C/C++, multi-stream batching, latency or throughput tuning, or C++ concurrency and lifetime design.
rules.why: Hardware-adjacent C++/CUDA design where subtle mistakes cost days; reserve the strongest reasoning. This host has no NVIDIA GPU, so workers must state what still needs verification on a GPU or Jetson device.

rules.when: Diagnosing hard runtime failures: segfaults, memory leaks or corruption, deadlocks, race conditions, GStreamer caps negotiation or pipeline stalls, DeepStream or nvinfer errors, CUDA errors, accuracy drift between PyTorch, ONNX and TensorRT, or any bug whose cause is unknown.
rules.why: Root-causing across Python, C++, GStreamer and CUDA layers needs deep reasoning before any fix.

rules.when: Well-specified C++ or build-system work: CMake or Makefile changes, compiler or linker errors, pybind11 or Python binding glue, packaging, Dockerfiles for DeepStream or CUDA images, Jetson or JetPack setup scripts, CI, shell, Ansible or automation with clear acceptance criteria.
rules.why: Bounded engineering with testable outcomes; Codex handles build and tooling work well.

rules.when: Python AI integration work with reasonably clear requirements: inference or pre/post-processing code, model export to ONNX, DeepStream Python bindings (pyds) probes and metadata handling, data pipelines, evaluation scripts, tests, code review, bug fixes with a known cause, documentation, or moderate multi-file changes.
rules.why: Balanced cost and quality for everyday Python and integration work.

rules.when: Mechanical, deterministic, low-risk and narrowly scoped edits: DeepStream or nvinfer config file tweaks, gst-launch pipeline string changes, label files, renaming, formatting, typo fixes, simple version bumps, file gathering, or small config changes.
rules.why: Minimize cost and latency for tasks requiring little reasoning.
